Introduction

A modern dishwasher can use less water than washing by hand – but only if it is loaded correctly and run on the right programme. The choice between an intensive 70 °C programme and an eco-programme can make a significant difference to your electricity bill and water use. In this worksheet you will investigate those differences and decide when each programme makes sense.
Theory
A dishwasher uses most of its energy to **heat water**. It also uses a small amount for the drying cycle (heating element).

**Intensive programme (70 °C):** Uses more water (18–20 l) and more electricity (1.5–2.0 kWh) – meant for pots and heavily soiled dishes.
**Auto programme:** Sensors adjust temperature and duration – convenient but often less efficient than Eco.
**Eco programme (50 °C):** Long cycle (3–4 hours) but lower temperature. Typical: 0.8–1.0 kWh, 10–12 l of water.
**Hand-washing comparison:** A running tap uses 6–12 l of water per minute. Washing dishes for 10 minutes with the tap half-open = 60–120 l – far more than a dishwasher.

**Eco label**: Since 2021, dishwashers have carried an EU energy label rating from A (best) to G. The label shows: energy per cycle (kWh), water per cycle (liters), noise level (dB), and programme duration.
**Half-load**: Running a half-loaded machine wastes energy and water. If you have a half-load setting, it typically saves 20–30% on both. Otherwise, waiting for a full load is more efficient.
